subject: coord_equal() or substitute names for numbers

messages.author: 76d98a0ca212dd76
messages.subject: coord_equal() or substitute names for numbers
parts:
greetings,

I'm trying to plot a grid. I need the x/y axes to be equal length per
unit. the columns are represented by letters similar to Excel. so
first position from the NW most bucket would be A1. I want to display
values associated with either colors or sized circles that draw the
attention of the viewer to areas in the grid that may have
predominately large or small values. I'm almost there but I can't
figure out how to replace the integers on the x-axis with letters
while retaining coord_equal(ratio=1) as a layer.

code so far:

dframe = data.frame(rows=rep(1:4,each=3),cols=rep(1:3,4),val=rnorm
(12)) # rows/cols/val
td = ggplot(aes(rows,cols,label=as.character(round(val))),data=dframe)
td + geom_text() + geom_point(shape=15,alpha=I(1/5),aes(size=20*abs
(dframe$val))) +coord_equal()

so the trick I'm missing is to change 1-4 in the x-axis to A-D.

thanks in advance for any help you can provide. and thank you for a
great graphing package.

-Carlo

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: coord_equal() or substitute names for numbers
parts:
Hi,

I don't know if coord_equal can work with discrete scales. You can set
the labels manually with scale_continuous instead,

dframe = data.frame(rows=rep(1:4,each=3),cols=rep(1:3,4),val=rnorm(12))
# rows/cols/val
td = ggplot(aes(rows,cols,label=as.character(round(val))),data=dframe) +
geom_point(shape=15,alpha=1/5,aes(size=20*abs(dframe$val))) +
geom_text() +
coord_equal()

td + scale_x_continuous(breaks=unique(dframe$rows),
label=LETTERS[unique(dframe$rows)])

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: coord_equal() or substitute names for numbers
parts:
excellent solution to the problem. thank you.

one more observation. calling coord_equal() does more than just assure
equally spaced coordinates. if say there are 4 columns and 3 rows as
per the example, it pads the rows to generate a square plot. and I
can't find a work-around for this issue. I've tried setting limits and
calling xlim and ylim with no luck.

it seems setting 'ratio = 1' in coord_equal should address the ratio
of x to y coordinates only and not force a square plot.

I was using 0.8.3. I updated to 0.8.5 under R version 2.10.1. and it
still manifests the same behavior.

e.g.
####### begin code

dframe = data.frame(rows=rep(1:4,each=3),cols=rep(1:3,4),val=rnorm
(12))

td = ggplot(aes(rows,cols,label=as.character(round(val))),data=dframe)
+
xlim(1,4) +
ylim(1,3) +

geom_point(shape=15,alpha=1/5,aes(size=20*abs(dframe$val))) +
geom_text() +
coord_equal()

td + scale_x_continuous(breaks=unique(dframe$rows),
label=LETTERS[unique(dframe$rows)])

####### end code

I end up with 0.5 and 3.5 in the y breaks and a square plot. I plotted
without the scale_x_continuous conversion and still padded and square.
